lines: Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century, perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the **scope** and seriousness of their arts coverage.
在过去四分之一个世纪里英语报纸发生的所有变化中，影响最为深远的，也许是其艺术报道的范围和严肃性无可挽回的衰退。

lines: It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers. Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews. To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-**circulation** dailies.
让四十岁以下的普通读者去想象一个大多数大城市报纸上都能读到高质量艺术评论的时代，实在是难上加难。然而，20世纪出版的最重要的评论集中，有相当大一部分主要就是由报纸评论构成的。今天读这些书，人们会惊叹：书中那些学识渊博的内容，居然曾被认为适合刊登在面向大众的日报上。

lines: We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an **ornament** to the publications in which it appeared. In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered. Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about. These men believed in journalism as a **calling**, and were proud to be published in the daily press. “So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism,” Newman wrote, “that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are.'”

对于20世纪初至第二次世界大战前夕英国报纸上那些不拘一格的评论，我们就更加陌生了；在那个年代，新闻纸便宜得几乎不值钱，格调高雅的艺术评论被视为其发表刊物的一种点缀。在那些遥远的岁月里，大报的评论家对自己所报道的事件作详细而深入的记述，被认为是理所当然的。这是他们的一项严肃事业；即便是那些不故弄玄虚的评论家，如萧伯纳和欧内斯特·纽曼，人们也相信他们深知自己所谈何物。这些人把新闻工作视为一种使命，并因作品能在日报上发表而自豪。纽曼写道：“有足够头脑或文学天赋、能在新闻写作中站稳脚跟的作者少之又少，以至于我很想把“新闻业”定义为“不受读者欢迎的作者对受欢迎的作者所用的蔑称”。”

lines: Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten. Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket. During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England's foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller. He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored. Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to **specialists**.

遗憾的是，这些评论家如今几乎已被人遗忘。内维尔·卡达斯从1917年起为《曼彻斯特卫报》撰稿，直到1975年去世前不久，如今人们只知道他是板球比赛的评论作者。但在他生前，他也是英格兰最重要的古典音乐评论家之一，而且文风深得人心，以至于他的《自传》（1947年）成了畅销书。1967年他被封为爵士，是第一位获此殊荣的音乐评论家。然而，他的书如今只有一本还在印行，而他卷帙浩繁的音乐著述，除了专业人士外已无人知晓。

lines: Curbs on business-method claims would be a dramatic **about-face**, because it was the Federal Circuit itself that introduced such patents with its 1998 decision in the so-called State Street Bank case, approving a patent on a way of pooling mutual-fund assets. That ruling produced an explosion in business-method patent filings, initially by emerging Internet companies trying to stake out exclusive rights to specific types of online transactions. Later, more established companies raced to add such patents to their files, if only as a defensive move against rivals that might beat them to the punch. In 2005, IBM noted in a court filing that it had been issued more than 300 business-method patents, despite the fact that it questioned the legal basis for granting them. Similarly, some Wall Street investment firms armed themselves with patents for financial products, even as they took positions in court cases opposing the practice.

对商业方法专利申请加以限制将是一次戏剧性的大转变，因为正是联邦巡回上诉法院自己通过1998年所谓道富银行案的裁决开创了这类专利，批准了一项关于共同基金资产汇集方法的专利。该裁决引发商业方法专利申请的爆炸式增长，最初是新兴互联网公司试图为特定类型的在线交易圈占专有权。后来，一些更成熟的大公司也竞相把此类专利收入囊中，哪怕只是作为防御手段，以防被对手抢占先机。2005年，IBM在一份法庭文件中指出，它已获得300多项商业方法专利，尽管它对授予这类专利的法律依据心存怀疑。同样，一些华尔街投资公司一边为金融产品申请专利武装自己，一边又在诉讼中反对这种做法。

lines: In his book The Tipping Point, Malcolm Gladwell argues that “social epidemics” are driven in large part by the actions of a tiny minority of special individuals, often called influentials, who are unusually informed, persuasive, or well connected. The idea is intuitively compelling, but it doesn't explain how ideas actually spread.
马尔科姆·格拉德威尔在其著作《引爆点》中提出，“社会流行潮”在很大程度上是由极少数特殊人物的行为推动的，这些人通常被称为有影响力的人，他们要么消息格外灵通，要么特别有说服力，要么人脉极广。这一观点在直觉上颇具吸引力，却并未解释思想实际上是如何传播的。

lines: The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the “two-step flow of communication”: Information flows from the media to the influentials and from them to everyone else. Marketers have embraced the two-step flow because it suggests that if they can just find and influence the influentials, those select people will do most of the work for them. The theory also seems to explain the sudden and unexpected popularity of certain looks, brands, or neighborhoods. In many such cases, a cursory search for causes finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention. Anecdotal evidence of this kind fits nicely with the idea that only certain special people can drive **trends**.

所谓有影响力的人的重要性，源自一种听起来颇有道理却基本未经检验的理论——“两级传播论”：信息从媒体流向有影响力的人，再由他们传给其他所有人。营销人员对两级传播论情有独钟，因为该理论意味着，只要找到并影响这些有影响力的人，这些精选出来的人就会替他们完成大部分工作。这一理论似乎还能解释某些发型、品牌或社区何以突然意外走红。在许多这类情形中，粗略地探究一下原因便会发现，早在别人留意之前，就有一小群人在穿戴、推广或发展那样的东西。这类轶事证据与“只有某些特殊人物才能引领潮流”的观念十分契合。

lines: The researchers' argument stems from a simple observation about social influence: With the exception of a few celebrities like Oprah Winfrey — whose outsize presence is primarily a function of media, not interpersonal, influence — even the most influential members of a population simply don't interact with that many others. Yet it is precisely these non-celebrity influentials who, according to the two-step-flow theory, are supposed to drive social epidemics, by influencing their friends and colleagues directly. For a social epidemic to occur, however, each person so affected must then influence his or her own acquaintances, who must in turn influence theirs, and so on; and just how many others pay attention to each of these people has little to do with the initial influential. If people in the network just two degrees removed from the initial influential prove **resistant**, for example, the cascade of change won't propagate very far or affect many people.

研究人员的论据来自对社会影响力的一个简单观察：除了奥普拉·温弗瑞等少数名人——其超凡的影响力主要是媒体影响力的产物，而非人际影响力——即便一个群体中最有影响力的成员，与之打交道的人其实也并不很多。而按照两级传播论，恰恰是这些非名人的有影响力者应当通过直接影响自己的朋友和同事来推动社会流行潮。然而，一场社会流行潮要发生，每个受到影响的人都必须再去影响自己的熟人，这些熟人又必须去影响他们的熟人，如此环环相扣；而这些人各自能引起多少别人的注意，与最初那位有影响力的人关系不大。例如，如果网络中离初始影响源仅两层的那些人表现出抵触，这场变化的连锁反应就传不远，也影响不了多少人。

lines: Building on the basic truth about interpersonal influence, the researchers studied the dynamics of social influence by conducting thousands of computer simulations of populations, manipulating a number of variables relating to people's ability to influence others and their tendency to be influenced. They found that the principal requirement for what is called “global cascades” — the widespread propagation of influence through networks — is the presence not of a few influentials but, rather, of a critical mass of easily influenced people.

lines: Bankers have been blaming themselves for their troubles in public. Behind the scenes, they have been taking aim at someone else: the accounting standard-setters. Their rules, moan the banks, have forced them to report enormous losses, and it's just not fair. lines: After a bruising encounter with Congress, America's Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) rushed through rule changes. options: [A] The first and more important is the consumer's growing preference for eating out: the consumption of food and drink in places other than homes has risen from about 32 percent of total consumption in 1995 to 35 percent in 2000 and is expected to approach 38 percent by 2005. This development is boosting wholesale demand from the food service segment by 4 to 5 percent a year across Europe, compared with growth in retail demand of 1 to 2 percent. Meanwhile, as the recession is looming large, people are getting anxious. They tend to keep a tighter hold on their purse and consider eating at home a realistic alternative.
[A] 第一种也是更重要的一种趋势，是消费者越来越喜欢外出就餐：在家以外的场所消费的食品和饮料，已从1995年约占消费总量的32%升至2000年的35%，并预计到2005年将接近38%。这一发展正使欧洲各地来自餐饮服务业的批发需求以每年4%到5%的速度增长，而零售需求的增速仅为1%到2%。与此同时，由于经济衰退日益显现，人们日趋焦虑。他们往往捂紧钱包，把在家吃饭当作一种现实的选择。

data.title: 图画作文：文化“火锅”，既美味又营养
data.directions_en: 52. Directions: Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following drawing. In your essay, you should 1) describe the drawing briefly, 2) explain its intended meaning, and 3) give your comments. You should write neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points)
data.directions_zh: 52. 题目要求：根据下图写一篇160—200词的文章。文章中，你应当：1）简要描述图画；2）解释其寓意；3）发表你的评论。请工整地写在答题卡2上。（20分）
data.image_desc: 图画题为“文化'火锅'，既美味又营养”：一口热气腾腾的火锅，锅里同时煮着各种中外文化元素——佛、功夫、莎士比亚、天鹅湖、京剧、道教、儒学、仁、毕昇、老舍、爱因斯坦、后现代、解构、人本等，象征中外文化的交融。
sample: The cartoon depicts a steaming hotpot, into which a dazzling variety of cultural ingredients are being put: Buddhism, Kungfu, Shakespeare, Swan Lake, Peking Opera, Taoism, Confucianism, the theories of Einstein, postmodernism, and many more. The caption reads: “The cultural 'hotpot' is both delicious and nutritious.”
这幅漫画描绘了一口热气腾腾的火锅，人们正往锅里加入琳琅满目的各种文化食材：佛教、功夫、莎士比亚、天鹅湖、京剧、道教、儒学、爱因斯坦的理论、后现代主义，等等。图的标题是：“文化“火锅”，既美味又营养。”

sentences.en: The caption reads: “The cultural 'hotpot' is both delicious and nutritious.”

sample: The symbolic meaning of the drawing is quite clear: in the age of globalization, different cultures, Chinese and foreign, ancient and modern, are being blended together like ingredients in a hotpot. Such fusion does not destroy the distinctive flavor of each culture; on the contrary, it enriches our cultural life and creates a new dish with its own unique taste. Just as a hotpot becomes more delicious with more ingredients, a nation becomes culturally more nutritious by absorbing the essence of other civilizations.
这幅画的寓意十分清楚：在全球化时代，中外文化、古今文化正如火锅中的食材一样被融合在一起。这种融合并不会破坏每种文化独特的风味；恰恰相反，它丰富了我们的文化生活，烹制出一道独具风味的新菜肴。正如食材越多火锅越美味，一个民族通过吸收其他文明的精华，其文化也会更有“营养”。
